methodology.name: Team FAIR-style Monte Carlo model
methodology.description: Each scenario combines event frequency, conditional success, and component-level primary and secondary loss. Launch-Day DDoS is measured per seven-day launch event; the other three scenarios are annual.
methodology.formula: Loss = material loss events x (primary loss + secondary-effect indicator x secondary loss)
methodology.sampling: Triangular low / most-likely / high inputs; 10,000 trials with fixed seed 20261124. Annual event counts use a Poisson draw on threat event frequency, thinned by conditional success.
methodology.controlRule: Each control multiplies only the factors it genuinely influences by (1 - effectiveness); effectiveness is sampled from its low / likely / high range and stacks multiplicatively. Baseline and residual runs share the same random draws, so differences come only from controls.
methodology.costRule: Launch event view charges the full first-year cost (one-time + annual + per-launch) to the launch event, a conservative choice. Annual view uses annual cost + one-time cost amortized over 3 years + per-launch cost x 1 launch per year.
methodology.disclaimer: This is a team-designed FAIR-style model for decision support, not an official Open FAIR, NIST, or MITRE assessment. It makes no claim about Take-Two's private controls or architecture.
methodology.timing: Inputs are an ex-ante estimate for the Nov 19-25, 2026 launch window. Launch-week observations (Rockstar services held; PSN disruptions on Nov 18-19) are used as calibration evidence. The same structure applies to the later GTA VI online and PC launches.
